jobs.title: Regional Executive Director
jobs.description:
Company Description
Heart of Grace Home Care is a nonmedical organization providing home-based care services to individuals and families in need of clinical and supportive care. Headquartered in Forest, MS, the company focuses on delivering compassionate, reliable services that help clients maintain independence and quality of life in their own homes. Heart of Grace Home Care collaborates with healthcare professionals and caregivers to ensure continuity of care and personalized service plans. The organization values integrity, respect, and client-centered care, offering team members an opportunity to make a meaningful impact in their communities.
Role Description
The Regional Executive Director is a full-time, on-site leadership role based in Forest MS. This position is responsible for overseeing regional operations, including staffing, compliance, financial performance, and quality of care across assigned locations. The Regional Executive Director will develop and implement strategic plans, monitor key performance indicators, and ensure adherence to regulatory and company standards. Day-to-day tasks include supervising and mentoring local managers, coordinating with clinical teams, managing budgets, and fostering strong relationships with clients, families, and community partners. The role also involves driving service growth, supporting business development initiatives, and promoting a culture of collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement.
Qualifications

Demonstrated leadership and management experience in healthcare, home care, or a related service-based industry.
Strong skills in operations oversight, budgeting, and performance management across multiple locations.
Knowledge of healthcare regulations, compliance requirements, and quality assurance practices in home-based care.
Excellent communication, relationship-building, and conflict-resolution abilities with diverse teams and stakeholders.
Proven capability in strategic planning, problem-solving, and decision-making in a fast-paced environment.
Ability to mentor and develop staff, promote a positive workplace culture, and drive organizational change.
Bachelor’s degree in healthcare administration, business, social services, or a related field; advanced degree or relevant certifications are a plus.
Willingness to work on-site in Brandon, MS and travel within the region as needed.

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
AIA Akron and Design Ohio–Akron-Canton seek a resourceful, organized Executive Director
to manage core operations for two professional membership organizations serving the architecture, design, construction, and allied communities of Northeast Ohio.

This is a hands-on, part-time association management role for someone who can move easily between Board support, member communications, event planning, sponsorships, financial administration, and day-to-day operations. The Executive Director provides continuity as volunteer leaders change and turns Board priorities into organized, completed work.

Position Details

Part-time:
Up to 20 hours per week
Work arrangement:
Primarily remote, with regular in-person events throughout the Akron-Canton region
Schedule:
Flexible daytime schedule, with periodic morning, evening, and occasional weekend commitments
Reports to:
The Boards of Directors of AIA Akron and Design Ohio–Akron-Canton, primarily through each organization’s President and Executive Committee
Compensation:
$25–$30 per hour, commensurate with experience

Required Qualifications

Three or more years of relevant experience in nonprofit or association management, operations, event planning, communications, marketing, membership services, or a related field.
Demonstrated ability to independently manage multiple projects, calendars, budgets, deadlines, and professional relationships.
Excellent writing, editing, communication, and organizational skills, with sound judgment and appropriate handling of confidential information.
Proficiency with common tools for email marketing, website updates, online registration, shared files, virtual meetings, spreadsheets, payment processing, and basic graphic design.
Availability for required meetings and events throughout the Akron Canton region, including some mornings, evenings, and occasional weekends, with reliable transportation.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience with membership associations, nonprofit Boards, sponsorships, or volunteer-led organizations.
Familiarity with Microsoft 365, Constant Contact, Square Online or similar platforms, online registration or membership systems, and graphic-design tools.
Familiarity with the architecture, design, construction, or allied-professions community.

Responsibilities

Support Board and Executive Committee meetings, including agendas, materials, minutes or decision records, action follow-up, annual planning, elections, officer transitions, and organizational records.
Plan and administer educational, networking, member, and community programs, including budgets, speakers, venues, contracts, registration, promotion, sponsorship, event operations, and closeout.
Administer applicable AIA continuing-education requirements, including attendance records, evaluations, Learning Unit reporting, and member questions.
Serve as a responsive contact for members, prospective members, sponsors, speakers, vendors, allied organizations, and the public; maintain membership records and support engagement, retention, and renewals.
Create and manage newsletters, invitations, announcements, promotional materials, sponsor recognition, websites, social media, registration pages, calendars, and email lists.
Support sponsorships and partnerships, including outreach, proposals, invoicing, benefits, recognition, and stewardship.
Support Treasurers with budgeting, reporting, invoices, payments, deposits, reimbursements, event closeouts, and recordkeeping in accordance with approved policies and authorization limits.
Maintain administrative systems, contracts, shared files, account access, confidential records, and organizational data; recommend practical workflow improvements.
Convert Board priorities into work plans, timelines, budgets, and measurable next steps.

How to Apply

Email your resume and a brief cover letter to
admin@aiaakron.org. Your cover letter should briefly describe your experience managing member-based organizations, programs, communications, and volunteer Boards.

Application deadline:
October 15, 2026

Finalists may be asked to provide relevant work samples and professional references.

Equal Opportunity

AIA Akron and Design Ohio–Akron-Canton are equal opportunity employers. Qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, or any other status protected by applicable law.
